landfill.title: How a landfill works

sentences.text: If you dig a pit and throw your trash in, you have a landfill.
But dirty trash juice leaks straight down into the groundwater you drink.
So you lay a thick clay base, but it is still not enough.
You add a thick black plastic sheet.
This is a landfill liner.
A pipe drains the collected juice into a tank beside the pit.
Sealed this tight, trash barely rots at all once it is buried.
A 1952 newspaper dug up decades later was still readable word for word.
But trapped trash still makes gas, so a pipe carries it out.
That flame is not waste burning, it is gas making electricity nearby.
Add a grass cap, a fence, and a few young trees.
Congratulations, you have built a landfill.

parts: trash juice seeping to the groundwater

sentences.text: If you dig a ditch along your house, you have a drain.
But one inch of rain on a small roof dumps over 600 gallons right by your walls.
The ditch floods.
Five feet down, that water pushes over 300 pounds on each square foot, and the wall cracks.
So you fill the ditch with gravel, but the water still sits at the bottom.
So you lay a pipe full of holes under the gravel.
This is a French drain.
Water seeps in through the holes, and the pipe slopes downhill to carry it away.
Wrap the gravel in fabric so mud can't clog it.
And the French in French drain is not France.
It is Henry French, a New England farmer and judge who wrote the book on drains in 1859.
Add the grass back on top.
Congratulations, you have built a French drain.
If you spray a muddy car with a hose, you have a car wash.
But the mud just smears on the paint.
So you build an arch with soap sprays and cloth strips.
But the soapy water runs into the creek.
So you cut a floor drain into an underground tank.
This is a water reclaim tank.
Sand sinks, oil rises, and clean water goes to a pump.
That pump sends up to 80 percent of the water back to the arch.
And a car wash does not waste more water than a hose.
It uses about 15 gallons of fresh water a car, but a hose can use up to 140.
Add a pay kiosk, a vacuum station, and a canopy.
Congratulations, you have built a car wash.
